faq.a: Samina is associated with the Arabic form ثَمِينَة, whose core sense is samina; precious, valuable (feminine).

faq.q: What is the origin of Samina?
faq.a: Samina is associated with Arabic. Samina is Arabic ثَمِينَة (Thamīna), the feminine of ثَمِين, meaning 'precious, valuable'.
Yes — the underlying form ثَمِينَة is Arabic.
Samina can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Samina should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Thamīna is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Samina mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Samina is rendered ثمینہ and carries the sense ثمینہ، قیمتی.

faq.q: What does Samina mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Samina is rendered ثمینه and carries the sense ثمینه، گران‌بها.
A romanized syllable approximation is sa-mi-na. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Samina?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Samina, samina. Script forms are ثمینه, ثمینہ, ثَمِينَة, समीना.

faq.q: Is Samina a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
